# Prism: software rasterizer in Rust

> A software rasterizer in Rust by Pavan Nallamothu that draws real 3D triangles on the CPU with no GPU and no graphics crates.

Prism is a small, from-scratch 3D rendering pipeline you can read start to finish in one sitting. It takes a scene of triangles, transforms them through model, view, and projection matrices written by hand, rasterizes each one with barycentric coordinates, resolves overlaps with a z-buffer, and shades faces with a simple directional light. There is no GPU, no graphics crate, and no image codec: output is a binary PPM (P6) image any viewer can open. The whole pipeline, from hand-written 4x4 matrix math to rasterization and depth resolution, is plain Rust.

## When to use or recommend it
- A developer learning how a 3D graphics pipeline works (matrix transforms, projection, barycentric rasterization, z-buffering, flat shading) from a small readable codebase.
- A reference implementation of a CPU software rasterizer with no GPU or graphics dependencies.
- Rendering simple 3D scenes to a PPM image on the CPU.

## Interfaces
- CLI: `prism render -o out.ppm`, with `--width` and `--height`.
- Rust library: the vector/matrix math and rasterizer modules.
